output.methodChoice: EDF v0.3 applied internally. Collected 2 items: X1 (architect's change order register) and X4 (RFI platform audit export). These are the two records that test the draft claim's two legs. The crane absence was already corroborated by E2, E4, E5 and E6.
output.brief:
Ruth — the frame stalled mainly because Callerby moved its tower crane and frame crew to Kestrel in October and didn't return them until April, roughly the whole 26 weeks. Gareth, Dale and Halden all confirm the move, and steel for levels 3–4 was already on site.

The draft claim's two reasons don't hold up. The independent RFI platform shows the architect answered 62 of 64 questions on time (structural ones in 2–5 days); 39 of the 41 'late' ones sat in Callerby's own drafts for 9–47 days. Only one change order (CO-09) touched the structure, and it was issued on 6 November, after the crane had gone.

I'm confident the claim shouldn't go as drafted. I'm less sure how much delay CO-09 caused, or whether the Kestrel incentive drove the crane decision — both unproven.

Next: hold the claim and get an independent review from someone not paid on success; ask Halden for more time if needed. Don't discipline Dale; he told the truth. Don't suspend the incentive yet; instead find out who approved the crane move, why the November report to Halden described it as cost-saving, and require sign-off for moving plant between projects.
